purpose: Public, reproducible evidence ledger for evaluating the NASA Burrows-Kurkov supersonic hydrogen-combustion benchmark as a P11.2B reduced-order heated-flow validation candidate. This ledger freezes only values directly exposed by NASA sources or exact unit conversions. It does not create an experimental Qdot-prime profile or claim finite-rate chemistry validation for the present solver.

primary_experiment.citation: Marshall C. Burrows and Anatole P. Kurkov, Analytical and Experimental Study of Supersonic Combustion of Hydrogen in a Vitiated Airstream, NASA-TM-X-2828, September 1973.
primary_experiment.copyright_status: Work of the US Government; NTRS marks public use permitted
confirmed_claims: The experiment used Mach 2.44 vitiated air at elevated temperature with hydrogen injection.
Detailed probe measurements of total temperature, pressure, and composition were obtained 35.6 cm downstream of hydrogen injection.
Ignition location varied with freestream temperature and is an experimentally observed quantity.

nasa_validation_archive.title: Burrows and Kurkov Supersonic Combustion: Study #2
nasa_validation_archive.role: NASA public unit/validation computation compared against Burrows-Kurkov experimental data

public_assets.repository_policy: Do not commit a fetched binary blindly; ingest through a manifest and retain checksum/provenance.
Use as authoritative computational geometry source after deterministic extraction; do not hand-copy dimensions from a plot.
Any one-dimensional field or heat-release quantity derived from this file must be labelled NASA_REFERENCE_SOLUTION_DERIVED, never EXPERIMENT_MEASURED.

source_conditions_raw.source_locator: NASA Glenn Study #2 Initial Conditions table and str_run.dat inlet/wall records

source_conditions_si.conversion_policy: Exact unit conversions only: 1 psi = 6894.757293168 Pa and T[K] = T[R] * 5/9.

experimental_targets.scope_note: The current repository solver can potentially compare reduced-order thermal/flow quantities such as Mach and total-temperature-related diagnostics after an admissible model reduction. It cannot claim validation of H2/H2O species profiles without species transport and chemistry.

nasa_reference_solution_record.boundary: Wind-US output is a computational reference solution. It may support a transparent reduced-order closure study but may not be relabelled as experimentally measured heat release.

reduced_order_promotion_policy.highest_permitted_target_scope: Prescribed-heat reduced-order validation against public NASA thermal/flow observables, with separate comparison to NASA Wind-US reference fields where derived quantities are used.
forbidden_claims: finite-rate chemistry validation by the present solver
species-profile validation by the present solver
experimentally measured Qdot-prime unless a direct experimental source is recovered
LBW/YBW classification from the Burrows-Kurkov case
silent replacement of the vitiated mixture with air properties
tuning heat release solely to force agreement with the exit Mach or temperature profile
required_before_formal_case: deterministic quasi-one-dimensional geometry mapping from the public NASA geometry/grid
explicit effective-gas or thermodynamic reduction policy compatible with the calorically perfect-gas solver
a non-circular prescribed line-heat-release closure with provenance, preferably derived from the public NASA reference solution and independently checked against experimental observables
ingested experimental exit targets with checksum and coordinate/units metadata
formal statement that species comparisons remain outside solver capability
